```{python}
#| label: fig-domain
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "GLORYS12 bathymetry with depth contours. Red outline: water at least 2000 m deep, connected through such water to the open North Atlantic, north of 10N."

import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("../code"))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, pandas as pd, xarray as xr
from IPython.display import display
from osim import gyre_mask as gm, osim_config as cfg

b = xr.open_dataset(os.path.join(cfg.GLORYS_DIR, "static_natl", "deptho_natl.nc")).sortby("latitude")
_f = gm.plot_domain(b.deptho.squeeze().values, b.latitude.values.astype(float), b.longitude.values.astype(float))
display(_f)
plt.close(_f)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-launches
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Launch positions of all floats with at least one profile in the domain (metadata, with 14 implausible entries replaced by the first profile). Blue lines: extended regions enclosing the given percentage of those floats' profiles over their whole lives, 1998-2026. Along each stretch of border a region reaches as far through water as the profiles that left the domain there, using a local distance quantile over a 300 km window of border; one quantile is solved per line so that it holds exactly that percentage of all profiles. Where no profile left, the line stays on the border."

launch = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(cfg.GLORYS_DIR), "argo_meta", "launch_domain_clean.csv"))
ext = xr.open_dataset(os.path.join(cfg.OUT_DIR, "domain_extent.nc"))
_f = gm.plot_launches(ext, launch, ext.attrs["inside"])
display(_f)
plt.close(_f)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-download
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Suggested velocity download, 0-70N, 90W-5E, against the domain and the extended region holding 99% of the profiles."

_f = gm.plot_download(ext, dict(lat=(0, 70), lon=(-90, 5)))
display(_f)
plt.close(_f)
```
